title: Shakshuka, light
summary: Eggs poached in a warmly spiced tomato and pepper sauce, loosened with spinach and finished with a little feta.

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Have the eggs, spinach and feta cheese within reach — once the sauce is ready it moves quickly.

Warm the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and salt and cook, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft and translucent and the pepper has lost its raw crunch.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin and smoked paprika. Cook for one minute, until the spices smell toasted — do not let the garlic brown or it will turn bitter.

Tip in the tomatoes, breaking up any large pieces with your spoon. Bring to a gentle simmer and leave uncovered until the sauce thickens enough that a spoon dragged across the pan leaves a brief trail.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, letting each wilt into the sauce before adding the next. Taste and adjust the seasoning.
Make four shallow wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover the pan and cook over low heat until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter over the feta cheese and parsley and bring the pan straight to the table.

storageNotes: Best eaten straight away. Leftovers keep 2 days in the fridge; reheat gently under a lid, though the yolks will firm up.

title: Shakshuka
summary: The classic pan of eggs poached in a rich, smoky tomato and pepper sauce, with feta and bread for mopping.

ingredients.name: white bread
ingredients.matchedDescription: Bread, white, commercially prepared (includes soft bread crumbs)

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Set the eggs, spinach, feta cheese and white bread nearby.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion, bell pepper and salt and cook until the onion is soft and translucent and the pepper is tender.
Stir in the garlic, ground cumin and smoked paprika and cook for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, crushing any large pieces. Simmer uncovered until the sauce is thick and spoonable rather than watery.
Stir the spinach through in batches until it has wilted completely. Taste and correct the seasoning.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook on low until the whites are just set.
Finish with the feta cheese and parsley. Serve from the pan with the white bread alongside for scooping up the sauce.

storageNotes: Best fresh. The sauce alone keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well — poach fresh eggs into it when you reheat.

title: Shakshuka, hearty

ingredients.name: white bread
ingredients.matchedDescription: Bread, white, commercially prepared (includes soft bread crumbs)

steps.instruction: Dice the onion and red bell pepper, mince the garlic and chop the parsley. Have the eggs, spinach, feta cheese and white bread to hand.

storageNotes: Eat fresh. The sauce keeps 3 days without the eggs and reheats well; add fresh eggs at serving time.

title: Greek yoghurt bowl, light
summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with berries, a little granola and a drizzle of honey — quick, cold and high in protein.

steps.instruction: Slice the strawberries. Spoon the greek yogurt into a wide bowl and spread it out so every spoonful will pick up some fruit.
Arrange the strawberries and blueberries over the yogurt, scatter over the granola, drizzle with honey and dust with ground cinnamon. Eat straight away while the granola is still crisp.

storageNotes: Assemble and eat immediately. Fruit and yogurt can sit together in the fridge for a day, but add granola only at the last moment.

title: Greek yoghurt bowl

steps.instruction: Slice the strawberries and banana and roughly chop the walnuts. Spoon the greek yogurt into a bowl and smooth the surface.

Top with the strawberries, blueberries and banana, then scatter over the granola and walnuts. Drizzle with honey, dust with ground cinnamon and eat immediately for the best contrast of creamy and crunchy.

storageNotes: Best assembled just before eating. Prepared fruit keeps a day in the fridge; keep granola and walnuts separate until serving.

title: Greek yoghurt bowl, hearty

Warm the almond butter briefly if it is stiff, then swirl it through the top of the yogurt in ribbons rather than mixing it in completely.
Arrange the strawberries, blueberries and banana over the top, add the granola and walnuts, drizzle with honey and dust with ground cinnamon. Serve at once.

storageNotes: Eat immediately for the best texture. Yogurt and cut fruit keep a day; add granola, walnuts and honey only at serving.

title: Overnight oats, light
summary: Oats soaked overnight with milk, yoghurt and chia, with plenty of blueberries and just a touch of maple syrup.

ingredients.name: semi-skimmed milk
ingredients.matchedDescription: Milk, reduced fat, fluid, 2% milkfat, with added vitamin A and vitamin D

steps.instruction: Tip the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground cinnamon and salt into a jar and stir so the chia is evenly spread rather than clumped in one corner.
Add the semi-skimmed milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup. Stir thoroughly, scraping the bottom, until no dry oats remain.
Fold in most of the blueberries, keeping a few back. Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until the oats are tender and the mixture has thickened.
Stir before eating, loosen with a splash of milk if it has set firmer than you like, and top with the reserved blueberries.

storageNotes: Keeps 2 days covered in the fridge. Stir well and loosen with a little milk before eating. Not suitable for freezing.

title: Overnight oats
summary: Creamy blueberry overnight oats with Greek yoghurt, chia and a swirl of almond butter. Made the night before, eaten cold.

Pour in the whole milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup and stir until the yogurt is smooth and every oat is wet.
Fold in most of the blueberries, then spoon the almond butter on top and swirl it through lightly rather than mixing it in.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until the oats are soft and the chia has thickened everything.
Stir once, top with the remaining blueberries and loosen with a splash of milk if needed.

storageNotes: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge, though the texture is best in the first two. Loosen with milk before eating.

title: Overnight oats, hearty
summary: A generous jar of overnight oats with extra oats, yoghurt and a proper spoonful of almond butter for a long morning.

steps.instruction: Stir the rolled oats, chia seeds, ground cinnamon and salt together in a large jar so the seeds do not gather in one place.
Add the whole milk, greek yogurt and maple syrup and stir firmly until the yogurt is fully worked in and no dry oats sit at the bottom.
Fold in most of the blueberries, then add the almond butter in small spoonfuls and swirl it through, leaving visible ribbons.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least six hours, until soft and thick.
Stir before serving, loosen with a splash of milk if needed, and finish with the reserved blueberries.

storageNotes: Keeps 3 days covered in the fridge. Stir well and add milk to loosen. Not suitable for freezing.

Combine the rolled oats and whole milk in a pan with a good pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer, stirring.
Cook, stirring regularly, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes, mashing in half the banana towards the end. If it stiffens too far, loosen with a splash more milk.
Spoon into bowls, add the peanut butter so it melts into the surface, and finish with the reserved banana and the cinnamon.

storageNotes: Best fresh. Refrigerated it sets firm; reheat with extra milk. Keeps two days.

title: Peanut butter and banana porridge, hearty
summary: A big bowl of oats with plenty of peanut butter, a whole banana and a scatter of seeds for a breakfast that lasts until lunch.

steps.instruction: Slice the bananas, keeping half back for the top.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for a minute until fragrant, then tip out.
Combine the rolled oats and whole milk in the pan with a good pinch of salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook, stirring, until thick and creamy, about 5 minutes, mashing in half the banana as it goes.
Spoon into bowls, add the peanut butter, and top with the reserved banana, the toasted sesame seeds and the cinnamon.

storageNotes: Best fresh. Keeps two days refrigerated; loosen with milk when reheating. Add the seeds after reheating so they stay crisp.

title: Turkish eggs, light
summary: Poached eggs over garlicky yoghurt with paprika butter and dill, with a wedge of bread for mopping.

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.matchedDescription: Bread, white, commercially prepared (includes soft bread crumbs)

steps.instruction: Stir the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt through the greek yogurt and leave it at room temperature. Cold yoghurt straight from the fridge will chill the eggs on contact.
Chop the dill weed and set aside. Toast the bread.
Bring a wide pan of water to a bare simmer, swirl it, and poach the eggs for about 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Melt the butter in a small pan with the paprika until it foams and turns deep orange, about a minute. Watch it — paprika burns fast and turns bitter.
Spread the yoghurt across two plates, set the drained eggs on top, spoon over the paprika butter and scatter with dill weed. Serve with the toast.

storageNotes: Assemble and eat immediately — poached eggs do not keep. The garlic yoghurt can be made a day ahead and refrigerated.

title: Turkish eggs
summary: Soft poached eggs on a bed of garlicky yoghurt, flooded with foaming paprika butter and finished with dill.

title: Leek and potato soup, light
summary: Sweet softened leeks and potato blended into a smooth, comforting soup, kept light with stock rather than cream.

steps.instruction: Slice the leek and wash it thoroughly in a bowl of cold water — grit hides between the layers and will not come out later. Peel and dice the potato.
Melt the butter in a large pan and cook the leek gently with a pinch of salt until completely soft and sweet but not coloured, about 12 minutes. Browning them makes the soup taste harsh.
Add the potato, thyme and vegetable broth, bring to a simmer and cook until the potato falls apart at the press of a spoon.

storageNotes: Keeps four days refrigerated and freezes for three months. Reheat gently and stir well, as it separates a little on standing.

title: Leek and potato soup
summary: The classic: leeks softened in butter with floury potato, blended smooth and enriched with a little milk.

Heat the sesame oil in a wide pan and cook the onion until soft and translucent, stirring now and then so the onion sweetens without catching.

title: Spanish tortilla, light
summary: A protein-rich Spanish tortilla with plenty of softly cooked onion, tender potato and eggs. Less oil and potato keep the lighter version balanced without changing its character.

steps.instruction: Slice the potato and onion thinly so they soften evenly without browning too quickly.
Heat most of the olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-low heat.
Cook the potato and onion gently until completely tender but still pale, turning them carefully from time to time.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl until the whites and yolks are evenly combined.
Drain any loose olive oil from the potato and onion, then fold them into the eggs.
Rest the egg mixture so the potato absorbs some of the egg and the tortilla holds together.
Coat the pan with the remaining olive oil and pour in the egg mixture.
Cook the tortilla over medium-low heat until the base is golden and the top is mostly set.
Invert the tortilla onto a plate and slide it back into the pan.
Cook the second side until golden while the centre remains tender and moist.
Rest the Spanish tortilla before slicing so it sets cleanly.

storageNotes: Serve warm or at room temperature. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently in a covered pan, or enjoy cold. Freezing is not recommended because the potato becomes grainy.

title: Middle Eastern beef kofta with tahini, light

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 220°C and heat a grill pan over medium-high heat.
Cut the eggplant into thick wedges and arrange it on a baking tray.

Roast the eggplant until browned at the edges and soft in the centre.
Mix the ground beef with the onion, garlic, remaining cumin, remaining paprika and half the cilantro.

Add the wheat flour gradually while stirring firmly to prevent dry pockets from forming.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C so the eggs begin cooking as soon as the dish goes in.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, garlic and spinach in their listed sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and cured pork until the vegetables soften and the pork edges colour.
Add the garlic and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and salt and simmer until the sauce is thick enough to hold shallow wells.
Fold the spinach into the tomato sauce until wilted.
Crack the eggs into the wells and bake until the whites are set and the yolks remain tender.
Rest the huevos a la flamenca briefly before serving.

storageNotes: Best served immediately while the yolks are tender. Refrigerate the tomato and pork base for up to 3 days, then reheat it and cook fresh eggs in the sauce.

title: Chicken fatteh, light
summary: Crisp pita, warm chickpeas and roasted chicken layered with lemony tahini yogurt. Extra cucumber and less bread and sauce keep this Middle Eastern lunch fresh and Mediterranean.

ingredients.name: chicken breast, skinless
ingredients.matchedDescription: Chicken, broilers or fryers, meat only, raw

ingredients.name: chickpeas, canned
ingredients.matchedDescription: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the pita bread into bite-size pieces and spread it across a baking tray.
Bake the pita bread until crisp and lightly golden.
Coat the chicken breast with the olive oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Roast the chicken breast until the breast is cooked through and lightly browned.
Warm the chickpeas, canned, in a small pan until hot, then drain them.
Whisk the greek yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, garlic and remaining salt until smooth.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until lightly golden.
Slice the cucumber and rest the chicken breast before cutting it into pieces.
Layer the pita bread, chickpeas, chicken breast and yogurt sauce in a serving dish.
Finish the chicken fatteh with the cucumber and pine nuts.

storageNotes: Best assembled just before serving so the pita remains crisp. Refrigerate the chicken, chickpeas and yogurt sauce separately for up to 3 days. Do not freeze the assembled dish.

ingredients.matchedDescription: Squash, summer, zucchini, includes skin, raw

ingredients.matchedDescription: Tomato products, canned, paste, without salt added (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)

ingredients.matchedDescription: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the onion, bell pepper, zucchini, garlic and cilantro in their listed sizes.
Heat half the olive oil in a saucepan and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth and half the salt and simmer until the enchilada sauce thickens.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a wide pan and cook the bell pepper and zucchini until softened and lightly browned.
Fold the black beans and remaining salt through the vegetables until hot.
Fill the tortilla with the black bean mixture and roll each one tightly.
Arrange the tortilla rolls in a baking dish and cover them with the tomato sauce.
Bake the enchiladas until bubbling and lightly crisp at the edges.
Finish the black bean enchiladas with the cilantro.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat covered until hot throughout. Freeze baked enchiladas for up to 2 months, although the tortillas will soften slightly.

title: Brazilian rice fritters, light
summary: Golden Brazilian-style rice fritters with eggs, parmesan, spinach and spring onions. Less rice, cheese and oil plus extra spinach keep the snack lighter and still satisfying.

ingredients.matchedDescription: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.matchedDescription: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then spread it on a tray to cool and dry slightly.
Prepare the spinach, spring onions and garlic while the rice cools.
Wilt the spinach in a dry pan until its moisture evaporates.
Mix the white rice, eggs, parmesan cheese, wheat flour, spinach, spring onions, garlic, paprika and salt into a thick mixture.
Shape the rice mixture into twelve compact fritters.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium heat.
Fry the rice fritters until golden and crisp on both sides, working in batches.
Drain the Brazilian rice fritters briefly on absorbent paper.

storageNotes: Best served freshly fried. Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot oven or dry pan. Freeze cooked fritters for up to 2 months.

summary: Torn Ethiopian flatbread tossed with fragrant paprika, cumin, ginger and garlic butter, served with cool Greek yogurt. Less butter and flour keep this breakfast lighter.

steps.instruction: Mix the wheat flour, water and half the salt into a soft dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates and becomes easier to roll.
Divide and roll the dough into two thin flatbreads.
Cook each flatbread in a dry pan until browned in spots and cooked through.
Tear the flatbreads into bite-size pieces while still warm.
Melt the butter with the paprika, cumin, ginger, garlic and remaining salt until fragrant.
Toss the torn flatbread through the spiced butter until evenly coated.
Serve the Ethiopian chechebsa with the greek yogurt.

storageNotes: Best served immediately while the flatbread is warm. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a pan with a splash of water. Keep the Greek yogurt separate.

Cook the onion, carrot and celery until the onion is soft and translucent.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a square baking tin.
Mash the banana until mostly smooth with only a few small pieces remaining.
Stir the peanut butter, brown sugar and cinnamon into the banana.
Fold the rolled oats and sesame seeds into the banana mixture until evenly moistened.

ingredients.name: bread
ingredients.matchedDescription: Bread, white, commercially prepared (includes soft bread crumbs)

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the potato, mushrooms, onion and bread in their listed forms.
Coat the potato and onion with the olive oil, paprika and salt.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to turn golden.
Add the mushrooms and butter to the tray.
Roast until the mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir the white beans into the tomatoes in a small ovenproof dish.
Place the bean dish on the roasting tray.
Bake until the white beans and tomatoes are bubbling.
Scatter the spinach across the hot vegetables.
Make shallow wells between the vegetables.
Crack the eggs into the wells.
Bake until the egg whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden.
Serve the vegetarian full English traybake with the toast.

storageNotes: Best served immediately while the eggs are tender. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently. Store the toast separately. Freezing is not recommended.

title: German cabbage soup with cured pork, light
summary: A lighter German cabbage soup with cured pork, potatoes, leeks and root vegetables in a thyme-scented broth. Extra cabbage keeps the lunch generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the cured pork, potato, green cabbage, leek, carrot, celery, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium heat.
Cook the cured pork until browned around the edges.
Cook the onion, leek, carrot and celery until softened.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Add the green cabbage, potato, beef stock and salt.
Simmer the soup until the potato and cabbage are tender.
Stir the sour cream into a ladle of hot broth until smooth.
Return the cream mixture to the soup.
Simmer the soup gently until creamy and evenly hot.
Rest the German cabbage soup off the heat.
Serve the soup with the cured pork distributed evenly between bowls.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently without boiling hard so the sour cream stays smooth. Freeze before adding the cream for up to 3 months.

title: Chicken saag, light
summary: Tender chicken breast in a smooth spinach, tomato, ginger and cumin sauce with a modest serving of rice. Extra spinach keeps this high-protein Indian dinner light.

ingredients.name: chicken breast, skinless
ingredients.matchedDescription: Chicken, broilers or fryers, meat only, raw

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.matchedDescription: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the chicken breast, spinach, onion, garlic and ginger in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a wide saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken breast until lightly coloured on several sides.
Transfer the breast pieces to a plate.
Cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika and salt and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chicken stock to the onion mixture.
Simmer the sauce until the tomatoes soften and the liquid reduces slightly.
Fold the spinach into the sauce until fully wilted.
Blend the spinach sauce until smooth.
Return the spinach sauce to the saucepan.
Stir the greek yogurt into the sauce until creamy.
Return the chicken breast to the sauce.
Simmer until the breast is cooked through and the saag is thick and glossy.
Rest the chicken saag off the heat so the flavours settle.
Serve the chicken saag with the white rice.

storageNotes: Refrigerate the chicken saag and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming. Freeze for up to 1 month, accepting that the yogurt sauce may need stirring after thawing.

title: Italian potato frittata, light
summary: A lighter Italian frittata with tender potatoes, spinach, basil and parmesan. Extra greens and less cheese and oil keep this Mediterranean breakfast generous.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Prepare the potato, spinach, onion, basil and garlic in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until just tender while the slices still hold their shape.
Heat the olive oil in a wide ovenproof frying pan.
Cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir until fragrant.
Fold the spinach into the pan until wilted.
Whisk the eggs, whole milk, parmesan cheese, basil and salt until evenly combined.
Arrange the potato evenly over the spinach and onion.
Pour the egg mixture into the pan.
Cook the frittata until the edges begin to set.
Bake until the centre is just set and the top is lightly golden.
Rest the Italian potato frittata before slicing.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and serve cold, at room temperature or gently reheated. Freeze individual slices for up to 1 month.

summary: Grilled chicken shish with peppers and onions, served with cool cucumber, dill and yogurt cacik. Less bread and oil keep this high-protein Turkish lunch lighter.

ingredients.name: chicken breast, skinless

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken breast, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, garlic, dill weed and pita bread in their listed forms.
Divide the greek yogurt between two bowls.
Mix half the greek yogurt with half the lemon juice, half the garlic, olive oil, cumin, paprika and half the salt.
Coat the chicken breast thoroughly with the yogurt marinade.
Marinate the chicken breast in the refrigerator.

Serve the Turkish chicken shish with the cacik and pita bread.

storageNotes: Refrigerate the chicken shish and cacik separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken gently and serve with freshly warmed pita bread. Freeze the cooked chicken for up to 2 months.

title: Chinese spring onion pancakes, light
summary: Flaky Chinese pancakes layered with spring onions and sesame oil, then pan-fried until crisp. Less flour and oil keep this vegetarian breakfast lighter.

ingredients.matchedDescription: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

steps.instruction: Mix the wheat flour, water and half the salt into a shaggy dough.
Knead the dough until smooth and elastic.
Rest the dough covered so the wheat flour hydrates fully.
Prepare the spring onions in their listed form.
Divide the dough into four equal pieces.
Roll each dough piece into a thin rectangle.
Brush each rectangle lightly with the sesame oil.
Scatter the spring onions and remaining salt over the dough.
Roll each rectangle into a tight coil.
Rest the coils so the dough relaxes.
Flatten each coil into a round pancake.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan.
Cook the first sides of the pancakes until crisp and golden.
Turn the pancakes carefully.
Cook the second sides until golden and the layers are cooked through.

storageNotes: Best eaten freshly fried. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a dry pan or hot oven. Freeze cooked pancakes for up to 1 month.

title: French salmon leek gratin, light

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Prepare the salmon, potato, leek and garlic in their listed forms.
Simmer the potato until just tender while the slices still hold their shape.
Melt the butter in a wide frying pan.
Cook the leek until soft and sweet.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Arrange the potato across the base of a baking dish.
Spread the leek evenly over the potato.
Place the salmon over the leek.
Whisk the heavy cream, whole milk, lemon juice and salt together.
Pour the cream mixture evenly into the baking dish.
Scatter the parmesan cheese over the gratin.
Bake until the salmon is cooked and the sauce is bubbling and lightly golden.
Rest the French salmon leek gratin before serving.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the chicken breast, potato, cucumber, bell pepper, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Mix the lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, paprika, thyme and salt into a marinade.
Coat the chicken breast with half the marinade.
Marinate the chicken breast in the refrigerator.
Coat the potato with the remaining marinade.
Roast the potato until nearly tender and golden underneath.
Thread the chicken breast, bell pepper and onion onto skewers.
Turn the potato wedges so they brown evenly.
Grill the first sides of the skewers until browned and lightly charred.
Turn the skewers.

Rest the chicken souvlaki so the breast stays juicy.
Serve the Greek chicken souvlaki with the lemon potatoes and yogurt.

storageNotes: Refrigerate the chicken, potatoes and cucumber yogurt separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken and potatoes until hot. Freeze the cooked chicken for up to 2 months.

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.matchedDescription: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the eggplant, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Brush the eggplant with half the olive oil.
Bake the eggplant until softened but still sturdy enough to fill.
Toast the pine nuts in a dry frying pan until lightly golden.
Cook the onion in the remaining olive oil until soft and translucent.
Brown the ground beef until no pink remains.
Stir the garlic, cumin, paprika and salt into the beef until fragrant.
Add the white rice, tomatoes, canned, and vegetable broth to the pan.
Simmer the filling until the rice is nearly tender and the liquid has reduced.
Scoop a little flesh from each eggplant half to make room for the filling.
Fill the eggplant halves with the beef mixture and pine nuts.
Bake the stuffed eggplant until the rice is tender and the tops are lightly browned.
Stir the greek yogurt with the lemon juice until smooth.
Rest the Middle Eastern stuffed eggplant before serving it with the yogurt.

storageNotes: Refrigerate the stuffed eggplant and yogurt separately for up to 3 days. Reheat covered until steaming. Freeze the baked eggplant without the yogurt for up to 2 months.

title: Korean beef patties with rice, light

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.matchedDescription: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched

ingredients.name: spring onions
ingredients.matchedDescription: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender and fully steamed.
Prepare the cucumber, onion, spring onions, garlic and ginger in their listed forms.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan until fragrant.
Stir the soy sauce, rice wine, brown sugar and sesame oil together.
Mix the ground beef with the onion, spring onions, garlic, ginger, half the soy mixture and half the sesame seeds.
Shape the ground beef mixture into eight flat oval patties.
Rest the beef patties so they firm slightly.
Cook the first sides of the patties until deeply browned.
Turn the beef patties carefully.
Cook the second sides until the patties are nearly cooked through.
Brush the patties with the remaining soy mixture.
Cook until the glaze is glossy and the beef patties are fully cooked.
Finish the Korean beef patties with the remaining sesame seeds.
Serve the beef patties with the white rice and cucumber.

storageNotes: Refrigerate the patties and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the patties gently in a covered pan. Freeze cooked patties for up to 2 months.

title: Mexican albondigas soup, light
summary: A lighter Mexican meatball soup with beef, rice, potatoes, carrots and zucchini in a cumin, tomato and cilantro broth.

ingredients.name: white rice
ingredients.matchedDescription: Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched

ingredients.name: zucchini
ingredients.matchedDescription: Squash, summer, zucchini, includes skin, raw

ingredients.name: vegetable broth
ingredients.matchedDescription: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

steps.instruction: Prepare the potato, carrot, zucchini, onion, garlic, cilantro and lime in their listed forms.
Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Mix the ground beef, eggs, white rice, half the onion, half the garlic, half the cumin, half the paprika and half the salt.
Shape the beef mixture into small round meatballs.
Cook the remaining onion in a large soup pot until soft and translucent.
Stir the remaining garlic, cumin and paprika into the onion until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and vegetable broth to the pot.
Bring the tomato broth to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato and carrot to the simmering broth.
Simmer until the potato and carrot begin to soften.
Lower the meatballs carefully into the broth.
Simmer until the meatballs are cooked through and the white rice inside them is tender.
Add the zucchini to the soup.
Simmer until the zucchini is tender.
Stir the cilantro and remaining salt into the soup.
Serve the Mexican albondigas soup with the lime.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently until the meatballs are steaming. Freeze the soup for up to 2 months; the potato and zucchini will soften.

Cook the onion and leek until soft and lightly golden.

steps.instruction: Prepare the pork loin, potato, carrot, celery, onion, garlic and basil in their listed forms.
Heat half the olive oil in a large saucepan.
Brown the pork loin on several sides.
Transfer the pork loin to a clean plate.
Heat the remaining olive oil in the saucepan.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery until soft and lightly golden.
Stir the garlic, tomato paste, thyme and salt into the vegetables.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and vegetable broth.
Bring the stew to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato to the saucepan.
Simmer until the potato is nearly tender.
Return the pork loin to the stew.
Add the white beans to the saucepan.
Simmer until the pork loin is tender and the broth is rich and spoonable.
Stir the basil into the Italian pork and white bean stew.
Rest the stew so the flavours settle.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently until the pork is steaming. Freeze the stew for up to 3 months; the potatoes will soften slightly after thawing.

title: Brazilian chicken and potato stew, light
summary: A lighter Brazilian chicken stew with potatoes, peppers and carrots in a bright tomato, paprika, lime and cilantro broth.

ingredients.name: chicken thigh, skinless
ingredients.matchedDescription: Chicken, broilers or fryers, dark meat, thigh, meat only, raw

ingredients.name: tomato paste
ingredients.matchedDescription: Tomato products, canned, paste, without salt added (Includes foods for USDA's Food Distribution Program)

steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken thigh, potato, bell pepper, carrot, onion, garlic, lime and cilantro in their listed forms.
Stir the paprika, cumin and salt together.
Coat the chicken thigh with half the spice mixture.
Rest the chicken thigh so the seasoning adheres.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a large saucepan.
Brown the chicken thigh on several sides.
Transfer the chicken thigh to a clean plate.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in the saucepan.
Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden.
Cook the bell pepper and carrot until they begin to soften.
Stir the garlic, tomato paste and remaining spice mixture into the vegetables.
Add the tomatoes, canned, and chicken broth.
Bring the stew to a gentle simmer.
Add the potato to the saucepan.
Return the chicken thigh to the stew.
Simmer the covered stew until the chicken thigh and potato are tender.
Simmer uncovered until the broth thickens slightly.
Stir the lime juice into the Brazilian chicken and potato stew.
Finish the stew with the cilantro.
Rest the stew so the flavours settle.

storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 3 days and reheat gently until the chicken is steaming. Freeze the stew for up to 2 months; the potatoes will soften slightly after thawing.
